skills.name: Singular and plural subjects
skills.description: The verb takes -s with a singular subject, not with a plural one.

skills.name: Agreement with tricky subjects
skills.description: Phrases between subject and verb; each/every/everyone.

ENG_PLURAL_VERB_S.label: Adds -s to the verb when the subject is plural
ENG_PLURAL_VERB_S.explanation: Writes 'the dogs barks', putting -s on both noun and verb.

ENG_NEAREST_NOUN.label: Makes the verb agree with the nearest noun
ENG_NEAREST_NOUN.explanation: Writes 'the box of pencils are' because 'pencils' is next to the verb.

ENG_EACH_PLURAL.label: Treats each / every / everyone as plural
ENG_EACH_PLURAL.explanation: Writes 'everyone have' or 'each of the boys have'.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that completes the sentence:  The dogs ___ loudly every night.
hints: Find the subject. Is it one thing or more than one?
With a plural subject (dogs, they), the verb has NO -s: the dogs bark.
solution: The subject is plural, so the verb has no -s.
The dogs bark loudly every night.

Each, every, everyone and nobody are singular.
solution: The verb agrees with the main subject, not the noun just before it.

sva_basic.title: Singular and plural subjects
sva_basic.big_idea: A verb must match its subject. One thing: add -s to the verb (the dog barks). More than one: no -s on the verb (the dogs bark). The -s moves from the noun to the verb, never both.
steps: Find the subject: who or what is doing the action?
Is it one (he, she, the dog) or more than one (they, the dogs)?
One: the verb takes -s or -es (barks, goes, has).
More than one: the verb has no -s (bark, go, have).
sva_basic.sense_check: 'The dogs barks' has two -s endings. Only one of the noun and the verb gets the -s.

worked_examples.prompt: My sister ___ to school by bus. (go / goes)

sva_tricky.title: Agreement with tricky subjects
sva_tricky.big_idea: Extra words between the subject and the verb do not change the subject. Words like each, every, everyone and nobody are singular.
steps: Cover up phrases like 'of the pencils' or 'in the box'.
What is left is the real subject: 'The box ... is'.
Each, every, everyone, everybody, nobody: treat them as ONE.
Read the sentence again with only the subject and verb.
sva_tricky.sense_check: 'The box of pencils are' becomes 'The box are' when you cover the middle. That sounds wrong.

worked_examples.prompt: The box of pencils ___ on the desk. (is / are)
Everyone in the class ___ a book. (has / have)
